name: finch-image-gen
description: Generate and edit images with OpenAI GPT Image 2.5 (or an OpenAI-compatible relay): text-to-image, image-to-image, masked edits, transparent backgrounds and custom sizes, right inside Finch.

scripts.build: node tools/build-icons.mjs && esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --platform=node --format=esm --target=node20 --outfile=dist/index.js && esbuild src/gallery.ts --bundle --platform=browser --target=chrome120 --outfile=dist/gallery.js && cp src/gallery.html src/gallery.css dist/
scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run typecheck && npm run build && npx @finchtoys/minitools doctor .

finch.name: 生图工具
finch.description: Generate and edit images with OpenAI GPT Image 2.5 (or an OpenAI-compatible relay), with a masonry gallery you can re-edit from: text-to-image, image-to-image, masked edits, transparent backgrounds and custom sizes.
finch.systemPrompt: Use image_gen_create to generate images with OpenAI's image API. Text-to-image: pass only prompt. Image-to-image / reference-guided editing: also pass reference_image_paths (local absolute file paths); add mask_path to limit the edit to a masked area. COST POLICY: unless the user explicitly asks for something better, keep the cheap defaults — model gpt-image-2.5-flare, quality low, size 1024x1024. Do not upgrade quality or resolution on your own initiative; quality goes low → medium → high → xhigh → max and both quality and size drive cost and waiting time. Only switch to gpt-image-2.5-sunburst when precise editing matters, and say why when you do. size takes 'auto' or WIDTHxHEIGHT (1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, 2048x2048, 2560x1440, 3840x2160 …). Set background='transparent' (with png or webp) when the user needs a cut-out. For a long, high-quality single render, pass partial_images 1-3 so progress stays visible. Generated images are saved locally as absolute file paths in the tool result and are also collected in the gallery (left sidebar App View, or the tool panel inside a session) — tell the user that when they ask where their pictures went; do not re-download or re-encode them, and use wechat_send or Session attach to show or share them. On older Finch builds, gallery edits arrive as image annotations containing the marked preview and complete request. Hosts with editable-text support instead attach the marked preview (red freehand strokes, numbered pins) as a plain image, with message text listing each comment, its percentage position and the ORIGINAL file path. Use the original path from the annotation or message text. Pass that original path in reference_image_paths, treat the attached marked image as the thing to change, and follow every comment without reproducing the red markup or numbered pins in the result. When the user instead writes their own request, follow that text and treat the attached image as the source. From the sidebar App View — which has no input box — the same edit arrives as a chat message with two images: the first is the ORIGINAL to edit and the second is the marked preview. If the tool reports the OpenAI API key is missing, tell the user to open the Image Tool entry in Toolcase, click its settings (gear) menu and choose "OpenAI API Key" to paste it in. That settings menu also holds the "API Base URL" for a proxy/relay endpoint instead of api.openai.com. The Image Tool button in the Composer toolbar sets the everyday generation defaults instead: default model, default quality and default size (a single image_gen_create call can still override model/quality/size, or base_url for a one-off endpoint). When a request is blocked or rejected, the tool returns the API error code and a remediation hint — follow the hint instead of retrying the identical request.
